title: `Variant::get_type_by_name` `HashMap` initialization is not thread-safe
body:
### Tested versions

v4.6.dev.custom_build [9dd6c4dba]

### System information

Godot v4.6.dev (9dd6c4dba) - Fedora Linux 42 (Workstation Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6600 (RADV NAVI23) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-12100F (8 threads) - 31.14 GiB memory

### Issue description

`Variant::get_type_by_name` uses a static `HashMap` to store the name->type mapping.  This `HashMap` is initially constructed as empty (thread-safe), then each call checks if the map is still empty, and adds the items if needed (not thread-safe).  If two threads call `Variant::get_type_by_name` at the same time, they can both see the map as empty, and both try to add the key/value pairs.  This can happen if both threads are parsing `Expression`s, and likely for some JSON methods, though I haven't tried with JSON.

This can cause a crash with a few different errors - I've seen one crash with `double free or corruption (out)` printed, one with `corrupted size vs. prev_size`, and one with stack trace below:

### Steps to reproduce

In a new project, add gdscript below to the main scene.  Running this script crashes around 1 in 10 times for me:

```gdscript
func _ready():
	var threads : Array[Thread] = []
	for i in 10:
		threads.push_back(Thread.new())
	
	for thread in threads:
		thread.start(_expression_test)

	for thread in threads:
		thread.wait_to_finish()

	print("Finished")

func _expression_test():
	var e = Expression.new()
	e.parse("Vector2(1, 2)")
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A, script above can be used in new project
